title: Checks for docstrings in which the first line does not end in a period.
summary: PEP 257 recommends that the first line of a docstring is written in the form of a command, ending in a period. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.68.
message_templates: First line should end with a period

title: Checks for docstring first lines that are not in an imperative mood.
summary: PEP 257 recommends that the first line of a docstring be written in the imperative mood, for consistency. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.228.
message_templates: First line of docstring should be in imperative mood: "{}"

title: Checks for function docstrings that include the function's signature in the summary line.
summary: PEP 257 recommends against including a function's signature in its docstring. Instead, consider using type annotations as a form of documentation for the function's parameters and return value. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.70.
message_templates: First line should not be the function's signature

title: Checks for docstrings that do not start with a capital letter.
summary: The first non-whitespace character in a docstring should be capitalized for grammatical correctness and consistency. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.69.
message_templates: First word of the docstring should be capitalized: `{}` -> `{}`

title: Checks for docstrings that start with This.
summary: PEP 257 recommends that the first line of a docstring be written in the imperative mood, for consistency. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.
message_templates: First word of the docstring should not be "This"

title: Checks for section headers in docstrings that do not begin with capital letters.
summary: For stylistic consistency, all section headers in a docstring should be capitalized. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.
message_templates: Section name should be properly capitalized ("{}")

title: Checks for section headers in docstrings that are followed by non-newline characters.
summary: This rule enforces a consistent style for multiline numpy-style docstrings. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.
message_templates: Section name should end with a newline ("{}")

title: Checks for section headers in docstrings that are not followed by underlines.
summary: This rule enforces a consistent style for multiline numpy-style docstrings, and helps prevent incorrect syntax in docstrings using reStructuredText. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.

title: Checks for section underlines in docstrings that are not on the line immediately following the section name.
summary: This rule enforces a consistent style for multiline numpy-style docstrings, and helps prevent incorrect syntax in docstrings using reStructuredText. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.
message_templates: Section underline should be in the line following the section's name ("{}")

title: Checks for section underlines in docstrings that do not match the length of the corresponding section header.
summary: This rule enforces a consistent style for multiline numpy-style docstrings, and helps prevent incorrect syntax in docstrings using reStructuredText. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.

title: Checks for docstring sections that are not separated by a single blank line.

title: Checks for docstrings with empty sections.
summary: An empty section in a multiline docstring likely indicates an unfinished or incomplete docstring. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.

title: Checks for docstrings in which the first line does not end in a punctuation mark, such as a period, question mark, or exclamation point.
summary: The first line of a docstring should end with a period, question mark, or exclamation point, for grammatical correctness and consistency. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.69.
message_templates: First line should end with a period, question mark, or exclamation point

title: Checks for docstring section headers that do not end with a colon.
summary: This rule enforces a consistent style for multiline Google-style docstrings. If a multiline Google-style docstring consists of multiple sections, each section header should end with a colon. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.74.
message_templates: Section name should end with a colon ("{}")

title: Checks for function docstrings that do not include documentation for all parameters in the function.
summary: This rule helps prevent you from leaving Google-style docstrings unfinished or incomplete. Multiline Google-style docstrings should describe all parameters for the function they are documenting. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.73.
message_templates: Missing argument description in the docstring for `{}`: `{}`
Missing argument descriptions in the docstring for `{}`: {}

title: Checks for @overload function definitions that contain a docstring.
summary: The @overload decorator is used to define multiple compatible signatures for a given function, to support type-checking. A series of @overload definitions should be followed by a single non-decorated definition that contains the implementation of the function. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.71.
message_templates: Function decorated with `@overload` shouldn't contain a docstring

title: Checks for empty docstrings.
summary: An empty docstring is indicative of incomplete documentation. It should either be removed or replaced with a meaningful docstring. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle and made it stable in v0.0.68.
message_templates: Docstring is empty

title: Checks for docstring sections that appear out of order.
summary: Docstring sections should follow the canonical ordering specified by the docstring convention (NumPy or Google). Consistent ordering makes docstrings easier to read and navigate. Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Section "{}" appears after section "{}" but should be before it

title: Checks for @property method docstrings that start with known verbs (e.g., "returns", "gets", etc).
summary: The Google Python style guide recommends that the docstring for a @property data descriptor use the same style as the docstring for an attribute or a function argument (e.g., """The Bigtable path."""), rather than a function-style docstring (e.g., """Returns the Bigtable path."""). Ruff takes this rule from pydocstyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Property docstring should not start with a verb ("{}")
